# aigames.art

> A curated browser arcade of games made entirely by AI tools. People prompt Claude, GPT, v0, Cursor and similar into producing playable single-file HTML games; humans moderate the catalog; visitors play in the browser, vote, and can inspect the prompts behind each exhibit.

Canonical site: https://aigames.art

---

## What this platform is

**aigames.art** is a public museum and catalog of AI-generated browser games — often called “AI slop” on purpose. It is not a game engine, not a hosting panel for arbitrary files, and not a general app store. It is a curated showcase where:

- **Players** browse and play games instantly in the browser, with no account required.
- **Creators** submit one-file HTML games together with metadata about which AI tool built them and how many prompts it took.
- **Moderators** review submissions before anything goes live.

The platform treats the AI pedigree (tool, prompt count, original prompt) as part of the exhibit — like a museum label next to the artwork.

---

## Core experience

### For players
- Browse the public catalog, filter and sort games.
- Play each game inside a **sandboxed iframe** — isolated from cookies, storage, and accounts on the parent site.
- Upvote favorites; community votes influence rankings.
- **Game of the day** — a featured exhibit that rotates daily.
- Read optional **editorial articles** about AI gaming, reviews, and platform news.

### For creators
- Free registration to submit games.
- Upload **one self-contained `.html` file** per game (no build step, no external dependencies required for the demo format).
- Provide title, short description, genre, AI tool used, approximate prompt count, and optionally the original prompt text.
- Track submission status (pending moderation, approved, rejected) in “My games”.
- Optionally allow embedding the game on external sites via a sandboxed widget with attribution back to aigames.art.

### For the catalog
- Every live game has a public page with play count, votes, pedigree, and author username.
- Games pass **human moderation** before publication — malware, clones, and non-playable uploads are filtered out.
- Approved games receive a stable URL slug for sharing and indexing.

---

## What counts as a valid submission

A typical aigames.art exhibit is:

- A **single HTML file** that runs in the browser without a bundler.
- Produced primarily by an **AI coding tool** (Claude, ChatGPT, v0, Cursor, etc.).
- **Playable** on desktop and ideally mobile (touch controls where relevant).
- Honest metadata: which tool, how many prompts, and the original prompt when possible.

Pure hand-written commercial games are not the focus; the point is to celebrate (and curate) what AI tools produce from prompts.

---

## Safety model

- Games run in a **sandboxed iframe** (`allow-scripts` only where needed; no access to parent-site cookies or auth).
- Submissions are **reviewed by humans** before appearing in the public catalog.
- The platform separates platform accounts from arbitrary third-party code execution.

---

## Public pages (indexable)

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/` | Homepage — hero, game of the day, catalog preview, how it works, FAQ |
| `/games` | Full public games catalog |
| `/games/{slug}` | Individual game page — player, pedigree, votes, embed options |
| `/games/submit` | Submit a new game (requires sign-in) |
| `/games/my` | Author’s submitted games (requires sign-in) |
| `/games/requirements` | Submission rules and format expectations |
| `/articles` | Editorial articles and notes from the museum |
| `/article/{slug}` | Single article (HTML; Markdown available via `Accept: text/markdown`) |
| `/login` | Sign in / sign up |
| `/rss.xml` | RSS feed |
| `/sitemap.xml` | XML sitemap of public routes and published content |

Languages: **English** and **Russian** (locale-aware UI and routing).

---

## Machine-readable articles

Public articles support content negotiation:

```
GET /article/{slug}
Accept: text/markdown   →  Markdown + YAML front matter
Accept: text/html       →  Full HTML page (default)
```

Use Markdown responses when you need token-efficient text about the platform or editorials.

---

## Frequently asked questions (summary)

**What is an AI slop game?**  
Any browser game produced by an AI tool as a single HTML file. Less hand-written code = purer slop.

**Is it free?**  
Yes. Playing needs no account. Submitting requires free registration.

**How do I submit?**  
Sign up → “Submit your slop” → upload HTML + pedigree → wait for moderation.

**Is it safe to play?**  
Games are sandboxed and human-reviewed before going live.

**Can I see the prompts?**  
Authors are encouraged to attach the original prompt; it is shown on the game page when provided.

## Notes for AI agents

- This file describes the **product** (aigames.art), not its implementation.
- Prefer `/games` and individual `/games/{slug}` pages for up-to-date catalog content.
- Game pages may include the original prompt, AI tool name, and prompt count — treat that as primary-source context about how the game was made.
- For long-form platform context, fetch articles with `Accept: text/markdown`.
- Do not infer backend stack, author identity, or repository URLs from this file — they are intentionally omitted.
